subject: Next steps: compatibility gaps & competitive checks

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow up

Evelyn — thanks for the demo earlier. Helpful to see the latency numbers and the routing knobs. A couple quick asks from our side as we triage migration risk: 

- Can you share a short slide deck that summarizes the compatibility gaps you saw in the call (API surface, prompt behavior differences, token accounting)?
- We want a CSV that maps our current OpenAI calls to the equivalent Redwood endpoints/params so our infra team can do a quick audit.
- High level: any known differences vs hyperscaler endpoints (resp. streaming, function calling, rate limits) we should flag to procurement?

Appreciate a single doc we can circulate to procurement and infra — Maria is copied.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, FinLytics
samir.patel@finlytics.io
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finlytics.io>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@finlytics.io>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intro + demo — follow up (compatibility gap summary + next tests)

Samir / Maria — thanks for the thoughtful notes. Attaching a short compatibility deck and an API mapping CSV as a starting point. High level recap below and proposed next tests we recommend running from your side (small infra-friendly checklist):

Quick summary (from our side)
- API surface: Redwood supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints for completion/chat + streaming and matches 1:1 for most parameters; differences called out in slide 2 (notably: batching semantics and preferred retry headers).
- Prompt behavior: minor tokenization diffs for emoji and leading newlines; we included a prompt-diff sample you can run locally.
- Performance: for long-turn chat with KV cache, Redwood's continuous-batching yields lower median p99 for token throughput in our benchmarks — see slide 5.

Recommended quick tests (we can provide scripts):
1) 10k prompt set run comparing token counts and logprobs (we provide script + sample prompts) — target: identify systemic token deltas > 2%.
2) Streaming parity check: verify chunk sizes and reconnection behavior for your 95th-percentile latency path.
3) Function-calling smoke: verify type round-tripping for 10 common schemas.

Attachments included: [Attachment: compat-gap-slide-deck.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)], [Attachment: api-surface-diff.csv (CSV, 42KB)], [Attachment: local-eval-plan.md (MD, 8KB)]

We captured owners below and suggested dates. Aditya / Grace — can you review the tech plan and confirm the scripts are runnable by Thurs?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finlytics.io>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intro + demo — follow up (compatibility gap summary + next tests)

Looping in a short technical checklist + how-to run the scripts from your CI: 

- local-eval-plan.md (attached) contains a dockerized test harness (python) that hits both OpenAI and Redwood endpoints and emits per-prompt diffs. It expects two env vars: OPENAI_KEY and REDWOOD_KEY.
- api-surface-diff.csv maps your current API calls -> Redwood query params (note batching vs single-request differences).
- Known deviation: token accounting can differ when prompts include combined system+user messages with embedded JSON — we included a normalization step in the harness.

If you want, we can run a joint session where we execute the 10k prompt job against a snapshot of one of your dev models; otherwise you should be able to run locally with the instructions in the MD. I can be on the call Thurs morning PST.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — the materials look good and the mapping CSV is exactly what procurement wanted. A couple of ask items from our side before we take this internal: 

- Can you add a short column in the CSV that states whether the Redwood call is covered by our existing IAM roles? If not, call it out as a migration lift.
- We also need a concise line item comparing costs of typical/steady-state token throughput between Redwood and the top hyperscaler (ballpark numbers for us to include in the SOW appendix).

Procurement will review on Monday; can we get the CSV update + a one-page cost note by Friday EOD? If you prefer, give us a ballpark now and refine after procurement sees the CSV.

— Maria
